records.specification_basis: The exact P60 cockpit photograph and accompanying description place the basic digital dash in the dashboard behind the wheel rather than in the rim. Visual inspection of the identified P60 cockpit shows a conventional closed circular racing rim. The exact-car cockpit photograph shows a round rim, matching the existing curated P60 works-car baseline. The GTR2 observation's D-shaped rim is therefore treated as an implementation-specific override. The first-person exact-car drive explicitly says downshifts need a throttle blip and no clutch. The exact-car drive explicitly describes driver throttle blips for downshifts. BMW's period specification, AUTO BILD's direct test, and Road & Track's exact-car drive all identify six forward gears. BMW specifies a straight-toothed six-speed manual gearbox and the exact-car drive explicitly identifies the original unit as a six-speed dog box. AUTO BILD calls the six-gear gate conventional H, and Road & Track identifies the restored P60 transmission as H-pattern. The period test describes a conventional H scheme and the exact-car drive confirms an H-pattern gearbox. BMW documents the race car's triple-disc carbon clutch, and the exact-car drive describes the clutch as necessary for getting off the line. Both direct driving sources describe clutchless running upshifts. The contemporary first-person test explicitly says the throttle must be lifted briefly for the clutchless upshift. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip.
